title: Running 4D Server as a Mac OS X "Faux" Service
author: Charles “Charlie” Vass, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: Mac OS X User Accounts Login Items
AppleScript application launching and shutdown handling
4DLink files for pairing 4D Server with a database
PairingsMaker utility database (included with the note)

historical_commentary.text: This note addresses a genuine historical gap: unlike Windows, older Mac OS X versions had no built-in mechanism to register 4D Server as a true background service, so the workaround used Login Items plus a paired AppleScript application to launch/quit the server. Modern macOS has since gained first-class facilities for this (launchd daemons/agents via launchctl and .plist definitions), which are more robust and are what 4D's own current server deployment documentation and most admins now recommend instead of the AppleScript/Login Items workaround described here.
related_updates: macOS launchd daemons/agents (launchctl + LaunchDaemon/LaunchAgent .plist files) are the modern, supported way to run 4D Server as a background service on macOS
4D's own current 4D Server documentation for macOS service/startup configuration supersedes this AppleScript-based technique
